column2: Two homes. The pricier one might be the better deal. Here's the one number that shows it.
Price per square foot. Divide the price by the built-up size, in square feet.
Home A: six hundred thousand for eight hundred square feet. That's seven hundred and fifty per square foot.
Home B: seven hundred and twenty thousand for twelve hundred square feet. Only six hundred per square foot.
So B costs more, but each square foot costs less. Compare like with like: same area, similar homes.
Landed home? Don't mix land area with built-up area. Use the same measure for both.
New launch? Use the nett price after any rebates. Then check transacted prices nearby, not just asking prices.
